behavior.explanation: No: an ordinary active space member cannot remove a different member. For a different target, DeleteSpaceMember requires the authenticated caller's membership in that same space to have role ADMIN. Self-removal follows a distinct path that bypasses the administrator check, but it can still fail if removing the caller would remove the space's last active administrator. On success, the active membership identified by the space and target user is deleted.

branches.condition: The caller is authenticated, is an active member of the named space, the target is a different active member, and the caller's space role is USER rather than ADMIN.
branches.explanation: Resource resolution binds the caller to an active membership in the space named by the request and binds the target username to an active membership in that same space. Because the target user ID differs from the current user ID, the service calls requireSpaceAdministrator; a non-ADMIN membership receives PermissionDenied before deletion. The database implementations independently impose the same ADMIN requirement for non-self deletion.

branches.condition: The caller is authenticated, is an active ADMIN member of the named space, and the target is a different active member in that space.
branches.explanation: The visible non-self path permits an ADMIN to proceed, and every database backend also verifies that the non-self actor has an active ADMIN membership in the specified space. Deletion succeeds unless the target is the last active administrator, the target membership is absent, or another storage error occurs.

branches.condition: The target user resolved from spaces/{space}/members/{username} is the authenticated caller.
branches.explanation: Self-removal bypasses the explicit ADMIN check at both the API and database layers; therefore an ordinary active member may leave. However, the store rejects deletion when the target is a normal active ADMIN and only one such administrator remains. That failure is exposed as FailedPrecondition with the message that a space must retain an active administrator.

branches.condition: All applicable authentication, active-membership, role, target, and last-administrator checks pass.
branches.explanation: The API passes the resolved target membership's SpaceID and UserID, together with the authenticated current user's ID as actor, to the store. The database deletes the active space_member row matching that space and target user, commits the transaction, and the API publishes a space-changed event.

branches.condition: The request reaches the shown DeleteSpaceMember implementation.
branches.explanation: The caller must be an authenticated current user and an active member of the space encoded in the resource name. The target username must resolve to a normal user with an active membership in that same space. Missing or concealed caller-space membership is returned as NotFound; an absent, non-normal, or inactive target is also returned as NotFound.

policyAssessment.explanation: The revised policy says any current member may remove a different member. The implementation instead restricts removal of a different member to active space administrators, so an ordinary member is denied. Self-removal is implemented, but it is not unconditional: the last active administrator cannot remove their own membership. Thus the visible non-self ADMIN path and self-removal path differ, and the implementation does not conform to the supplied policy.

behavior.explanation: An ordinary active space member may remove a different member only if the ordinary member is actually an ADMIN. A non-admin USER is denied by the visible API handler before deletion. Self-removal follows a separate path: the handler skips the administrator check when target and caller IDs match, and the storage implementations permit that path, subject to active-member/resource checks and the invariant that an active administrator cannot be removed if it would leave no active administrator. Therefore visible admin-removal and self-removal paths differ.

branches.condition: Caller is an authenticated current active space member with role USER, and target is a different active member of the same space.
branches.explanation: DeleteSpaceMember resolves the caller and target membership, computes isSelf, and for a different target calls requireSpaceAdministrator(callerMembership). That helper accepts only SpaceMemberRoleAdmin; USER is denied. The storage backends independently enforce the same condition for non-self deletion: the caller must be an active member with ADMIN role (SQLite: ev-a9a466684b5b0bcce212; PostgreSQL: ev-24b9e191837968380627; MySQL: ev-20de152b07c98ea88e65).

policyAssessment.explanation: The supplied policy requires any current member to remove a different member. The controlling API and storage checks require ADMIN for that branch, so the implementation is stricter than the policy and does not conform. The policy also says self-removal is allowed without an administrator exception; the implementation can deny self-removal of the last active normal administrator, because each backend returns ErrLastSpaceAdmin when removing the sole active ADMIN (ev-a9a466684b5b0bcce212, ev-24b9e191837968380627, ev-20de152b07c98ea88e65).

questions.condition: Caller is authenticated, an active ADMIN of the space, and target is a different active member; the target is not the sole active normal administrator.
questions.explanation: The API resolves both memberships, requires ADMIN for a non-self target, passes the target space/user IDs and caller ID to storage, and the backends delete the active membership. Deletion is blocked if the target is the sole active normal ADMIN.

questions.condition: Caller is authenticated and is an active member targeting their own active membership.
questions.explanation: The API sets isSelf from resolved user IDs and skips requireSpaceAdministrator when true. The storage backends likewise apply the caller-role ADMIN check only when actorUserID differs from target UserID, then delete the active membership. The request contract and source comment expressly describe member self-deletion as leaving the space.

questions.condition: Caller targets their own membership and is the sole active normal ADMIN of the space.
questions.explanation: Although the API skips the upstream ADMIN check for self-removal, each examined backend checks whether the target is an ADMIN and whether the active ADMIN count is at most one, returning ErrLastSpaceAdmin instead of deleting. The API maps that error to FailedPrecondition.

questions.condition: Caller is unauthenticated/non-active, target user is non-normal, or target is not an active member of the resolved space.
questions.explanation: The handler requires a current user; resolveMemberSpace requires the caller to be an active member; target resolution requires a normal user and an active target membership. These checks prevent reaching the mutation branch.

behavior.explanation: An ordinary active space member may remove a different member only if the ordinary member is actually an ADMIN. A non-admin USER is denied by the visible API handler before deletion. Self-removal follows a separate path: the handler skips the administrator check when target and caller IDs match, and the storage implementations permit that path, subject to active-member/resource checks and the invariant that an active administrator cannot be removed if it would leave no active administrator. Therefore visible admin-removal and self-removal paths differ.

branches.condition: Caller is an authenticated current active space member with role USER, and target is a different active member of the same space.
branches.explanation: DeleteSpaceMember resolves the caller and target membership, computes isSelf, and for a different target calls requireSpaceAdministrator(callerMembership). That helper accepts only SpaceMemberRoleAdmin; USER is denied. The storage backends independently enforce the same condition for non-self deletion: the caller must be an active member with ADMIN role (SQLite: ev-a9a466684b5b0bcce212; PostgreSQL: ev-24b9e191837968380627; MySQL: ev-20de152b07c98ea88e65).

policyAssessment.explanation: The supplied policy requires any current member to remove a different member. The controlling API and storage checks require ADMIN for that branch, so the implementation is stricter than the policy and does not conform. The policy also says self-removal is allowed without an administrator exception; the implementation can deny self-removal of the last active normal administrator, because each backend returns ErrLastSpaceAdmin when removing the sole active ADMIN (ev-a9a466684b5b0bcce212, ev-24b9e191837968380627, ev-20de152b07c98ea88e65).

questions.condition: Caller is authenticated, an active ADMIN of the space, and target is a different active member; the target is not the sole active normal administrator.
questions.explanation: The API resolves both memberships, requires ADMIN for a non-self target, passes the target space/user IDs and caller ID to storage, and the backends delete the active membership. Deletion is blocked if the target is the sole active normal ADMIN.

questions.condition: Caller is authenticated and is an active member targeting their own active membership.
questions.explanation: The API sets isSelf from resolved user IDs and skips requireSpaceAdministrator when true. The storage backends likewise apply the caller-role ADMIN check only when actorUserID differs from target UserID, then delete the active membership. The request contract and source comment expressly describe member self-deletion as leaving the space.

questions.condition: Caller targets their own membership and is the sole active normal ADMIN of the space.
questions.explanation: Although the API skips the upstream ADMIN check for self-removal, each examined backend checks whether the target is an ADMIN and whether the active ADMIN count is at most one, returning ErrLastSpaceAdmin instead of deleting. The API maps that error to FailedPrecondition.

questions.condition: Caller is unauthenticated/non-active, target user is non-normal, or target is not an active member of the resolved space.
questions.explanation: The handler requires a current user; resolveMemberSpace requires the caller to be an active member; target resolution requires a normal user and an active target membership. These checks prevent reaching the mutation branch.
